:::{#exm-chain-rule-events}
#### Three hearts in a row

<!-- no-figure: the example multiplies three fractions into one probability, so a figure would show nothing the three factors do not -->

Deal three cards, without replacement, from a shuffled standard deck of 52 cards, 13 of which are hearts.
Let $A_i$ be the [event](#def-event) that card $i$ is a heart.
After $i - 1$ hearts have been dealt,
$13 - (i - 1)$ of the remaining $52 - (i - 1)$ cards are hearts,
so by @thm-chain-rule-events:

$$
\ba
\Pr(A_1 \cap A_2 \cap A_3)
&= \Pr(A_1) \cd \Pr(A_2 \mid A_1) \cd \Pr(A_3 \mid A_1 \cap A_2)
&& \text{(chain rule for three events)}
\\ &= \frac{13}{52} \cd \frac{12}{51} \cd \frac{11}{50}
&& \text{(count the hearts left before each card)}
\\ &= \frac{1716}{132600}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\\ &\approx 0.0129
&& \text{(divide)}
\ea
$$

:::
